transformations: CSV category labels mapped to historical public names; intercept and named structural features separated from lexical terms.
Spanish PERMA restored from original UTF-8 WWBP CSV rather than corrupted legacy JSON.
Optimism is the intersection of historical future-term allowlist and canonical affect weights; an experimental composition, not a separately trained model.
Big Five and Dark Triad retain historical repository weights, except that Big Five N weights are negated: their signs described emotional stability, contrary to Schwartz et al. (2013).
Terms that the Happier Fun Tokenizer cannot produce are removed: PERMA spreadsheet errors #NAME?, #REF! and Err:508; Big Five '', ' -', ': ', 'the lord,', '93.00%' and '0.93%'.
PERMA 'TRUE' (spreadsheet boolean conversion) is restored to 'true'.
UTF-8 terms mis-decoded as cp1252 are repaired, e.g. 'â™¥' to '♥' and 'don â€™ t' to 'don ’ t' (age, gender, PERMA).
Doubled backslashes in affect, age and gender terms, e.g. ':\\', are restored to the single-backslash HFT tokens they escape.
Temporal orientation uses binary encoding, following the per-message binary ngram indicators of Schwartz et al. (2015) and Park et al. (2016).
Default ngram sizes are the token counts of the vocabulary under HFT, where spaced dots ('. . .') are one token; age and gender are therefore unigram-only, as in Sap et al. (2014).
The tokenizer is a port of the pinned DLATK Happier Fun Tokenizer; scripts/dlatk-reference.py executes that file only to regenerate test fixtures.
